newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech finmin plans further sell-off of major banks. [CORRECTED 12:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Czech finmin plans further sell-off of major banks. [CORRECTED 12:00 GMT]

text.p: The Czech finance ministry, charged with accelerating the privatisation of key state-held companies, said on Tuesday that it planned to begin the further sell-off of shares in banks Komercni Banka a.s. and Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s. this year.

Igor Fojtik, the director of the ministry's privatisation department, also told Reuters that the further privatisation of shares in the largest retail savings bank, Ceska Sporitelna was not planned for this year but possibly for 1998.

"This year, the beginning of privatisation of (16 regional gas and electricity) distribution companies, CSOB and Komercni Banka, three coal mining companies, (pharmaceutical producer) Leciva, and the partial privatisation of (radio transmitter Ceske Radiokomunikace, and tin producer Valcovny Plechu is planned," Fojtik said.
"We are not expecting that Sporitelna would go through (further) privatisation this year. That will evidently come next year," he added.

The finance ministry plans, expected to be debated for final approval later this month by the full cabinet, come as the centre-right government promised to speed up privatisations to build more efficiency into the country's slowing economy.
The CSOB and Komercni privatisations would entail partial stakes being sold through public tenders with other stakes placed on domestic and foreign capital markets.

The latest ministry plan calls for the sell-off of a 15 percent stake in each energy distribution firm through public tenders this year (corrects to add the words "energy distribution"), with the remainder being sold in 1998.
The government's long-awaited privatisation of the 16 regional energy distributors has been delayed several times.
Fojtik said the three coal mining companies to be privatised would be Mostecka Uhelna, Severoceske Doly, and Sokolovska Uhelna, but not OKD a.s., another of the largest.
